units.source: Geo Map
units.context: Geo Map

units.source: This note type displays the children notes on a geographical map, based on an attribute. It is also possible to add new notes at a specific location using the built-in interface.
units.context: Geo Map

units.source: Features__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Add markers on the map, which can be customized with icons, colors and text.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Search the notes already on the map, and look up places anywhere in the world.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Turn a place the map already shows into a marker by clicking it.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Draw paths, areas, rectangles and circles onto the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Display tracks on the map using __TRILIUM_PH_0__ files.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: Show your own location on the map and follow it as you move.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: 3D view of the map, which displays buildings when using a vector map.
units.context: Geo Map > Features

units.source: System requirements__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > System requirements

units.source: Starting with v0.105.0, the geomap uses MapLibre GL which requires WebGL v1 support. In general, most devices will support it because browsers/Electron can render it in software if needed.
units.context: Geo Map > System requirements

units.source: If the map could not be drawn because WebGL could not be initialized, an error message will appear instead of the map (__TRILIUM_PH_0__This map can't be drawn because WebGL isn't available…__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: Geo Map > System requirements

units.source: The button that shows your location is offered only when Trilium is reached over HTTPS, in the desktop application or in the mobile application. Browsers refuse to share the location of a device with a page served over plain HTTP, so on such a server the button does not appear. The desktop application on Linux does not offer it either, because it has no way to find the location of the device there.
units.context: Geo Map > System requirements

units.source: Interaction__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: At the top-left there is the search bar. It searches the notes already on the map, and it can also search for places online when you ask it to. While you move through the results of a search, a counter with previous (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and next (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) buttons appears under it.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: At the bottom-center there is a central toolbar which provides editing features: adding new markers on the map (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and importing GPX tracks (__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: At the bottom-right there are the viewport items:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: Zoom in/out (__TRILIUM_PH_0__ / __TRILIUM_PH_1__)
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: On mobile these are hidden, use pinch to zoom instead.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: On desktop, alternatively use the scroll wheel to adjust the zoom.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button that shows your location on the map and follows it (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Going to your location__TRILIUM_PH_2__ below).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Full screen button which focuses the entire map onto the screen, while still allowing for edits.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: At the top-center (on desktop, or left-center on mobile and in split views) there are the drawing tools such as paths, areas, rectangles and circles.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: When the map is read-only, the toolbar is not shown.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction

units.source: Creating a new geo map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: By default the map will be empty and will show the entire world.
units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: Repositioning the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: Click and drag the map in order to move across the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: Use the mouse wheel, two-finger gesture on a touchpad or the +/- buttons on the bottom-right to adjust the zoom.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: The position on the map and the zoom are saved inside the map note and restored when visiting again the note.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: A map that has no position saved yet is framed around the markers it contains when you open it, so they are all in view without having to go looking for them. A map that contains no markers shows the whole world instead.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: In practice this applies to maps whose markers were added externally, by a script or through __TRILIUM_PH_0__ETAPI (REST API)__TRILIUM_PH_1__. When you add markers yourself you have already moved the map to reach the place you are marking, and that movement saves a position.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning the map

units.source: Going to your location__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show your location__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the bottom-right of the map, beside the zoom buttons. The first time, the browser or the operating system asks whether Trilium may know where the device is. In the desktop application the operating system's location settings decide.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: The map then moves to where the device is and marks it with a blue dot. A lighter circle around the dot shows how accurate the position is: a phone with GPS gives a dot on the street, while a computer located through its network connection can give a circle that covers a neighbourhood. The map follows the dot as it moves, and the button stays pressed while it does.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Dragging the map stops it from following. The dot stays and keeps moving, and pressing the button again brings the map back to it. Pressing the button while the map is following turns the dot off.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Click the dot to see its coordinates in the panel a searched place is shown in. From there the position can be kept as a marker (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keeping a place as a marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__). Clicking the lighter circle around the dot is a click on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: If the position cannot be found, a message says so and the button keeps waiting for one; press it again to stop. If you refuse the permission, the button is disabled until the map is opened again. To allow it after all, change the permission for Trilium in the browser or in the system's location settings.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Your position is not stored in the note, and Trilium does not send it anywhere on its own. Moving the map there does what any other pan or zoom does: the tile provider behind the map's style sees the coordinates of the area now on screen. The map does remember where you left it, as it does after any other movement, so a map you have taken to your location opens there the next time.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Searching the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map

units.source: The search bar at the top-left of the map searches in two places. It always searches the notes that are already on the map. It can also search for places online, but only when you ask it to.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map

units.source: Searching the notes already on the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map

units.source: Type in the search bar, and the notes on the map are matched by their title as you type. Accents are ignored, both in what you type and in the titles, so __TRILIUM_PH_0__ finds __TRILIUM_PH_1__Zürich Hauptbahnhof__TRILIUM_PH_2__. Each word is searched for on its own, so __TRILIUM_PH_3__ finds __TRILIUM_PH_4__Paris Hotel__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Notes without a __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attribute are not offered, since there would be nowhere to go. Drawn shapes and GPS tracks are offered, even though they carry no such attribute: selecting one brings the whole shape or route into view.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map

units.source: If more notes match than the list can show, you are offered the ones closest to the area you are viewing.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map

units.source: Searching for places online__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: Looking up a place sends what you typed to a third-party service. For this reason, it never happens while you type. Instead, the last row of the result list offers the search. That row reads __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search online for "…"__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with the name of the service below it. The search runs only when you press that row or select it with Enter.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: Trilium uses Nominatim, the place search run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation. It needs no account and no API key. Its name is shown on every row that belongs to it: the row that offers the search, the row that says a search is running, and the row that reports that nothing was found or that the service could not be reached.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: The search prefers the area you are viewing. Places inside the current view are searched for first and listed above the others. If you search for a shop while looking at your own town, you therefore find the branch in that town, and not one with the same name on another continent. The view is always treated as at least 25 km across, so a search made while zoomed into a single street still covers the town around it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: Going to a point__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: If you type or paste coordinates into the search bar, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Go to__TRILIUM_PH_1__ row is offered above all the other results. Selecting it moves the map to that exact spot and marks it. You can then keep it as a marker, in the same way you keep a place found by searching.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: Points are untitled by default; the corresponding note opens with the default name selected so it can be easily replaced. If the map has a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ label, the marker is named by that template instead.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: The supported forms are:
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: A plain pair, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__. This is what Google Maps and OpenStreetMap both give you when you ask for the coordinates of a place, and it is also what the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ attribute holds.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ link that the map itself offers for a place, through the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Open location__TRILIUM_PH_2__ action.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: The address of a place on Google Maps or OpenStreetMap, pasted whole.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: A pair that is not a place on Earth, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, is not offered.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: Reading the results__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: Results are gathered under headings, and each group is ordered by distance from the middle of the map:
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__On this map__TRILIUM_PH_1__: notes that are already on the map, whatever their distance.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Nearby__TRILIUM_PH_1__: places found within about 25 km of the view.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Far away__TRILIUM_PH_1__: all the other places.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: The headings only appear when at least two of the three groups contain something. Every row that has a position shows how far away it is, in kilometres or miles according to your locale. A place found online shows its name on the first line and its address on the second.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: Selecting a result__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Selecting a note already on the map moves to its marker and opens the note beside the map, as clicking the marker would.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Selecting a place found online moves the map to it and marks it with a temporary pin. The pin has a different color from the map's own markers. The map is fitted to the area that the place covers, so a country fills the view, while a house is shown at street level. Some places have a boundary, such as a country, a county or a park. When the service reports one, that boundary is outlined under the pin.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: A panel then opens with the place's full address and its coordinates: in the top-right corner on desktop, and at the bottom of the map on mobile, where the top is kept for the search bar and the result counter. Pressing the coordinates copies them to the clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Keeping a place as a marker__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add as marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in that panel to keep the place. A child note is created under the map. It takes the name of the place, as well as the icon, which matches the kind of place it is. Its __TRILIUM_PH_2__ attribute is already set. The note opens beside the map, so you can edit it straight away. The temporary pin disappears, because the place is now a marker like any other.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: The button is not offered on a map that cannot be edited, where the panel can still be read.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: Press the panel's close button, or the Escape key, to send the place away without keeping it. The pin goes with it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: Stepping through the results__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Stepping through the results

units.source: Once you select a result, a counter appears under the search bar, with a previous (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and a next (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) button. These buttons move through everything the search offered, in the order it was listed. You can therefore compare several results without opening the list again. Pressing the counter itself moves the map back to the current result, which is useful after you have moved the map away from it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Stepping through the results

units.source: The keyboard__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ runs the online search when its row is the one selected, and otherwise moves to the highlighted result. Pressed after a result has been taken, it brings the list back.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_1__ closes the result list, and closes the place panel.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: Returning to the search bar reopens the list it was showing.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the end of the bar empties it, which also takes a searched place, its pin and its panel off the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: Adding a marker using the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map

units.source: Adding a new note using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button__TRILIUM_PH_2__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: To create a marker, first navigate to the desired point on the map. Then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the center-bottom of the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Once pressed, the map will enter in the insert mode, as illustrated by the notification. Additionally, a preview of the marker will be shown at the cursor position.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Simply click the point on the map where to place the marker. To cancel, press either the  Escape key or press again the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Once clicked, the marker will show up on the map and a popup will show to the right with the title already selected to be changed.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Adding a new note using the contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.source: Right click anywhere on the map, where to place the newly created marker (and corresponding note).
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.source: Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add a marker at this location__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.source: Once clicked on a position on the map, the marker will show up on the map and a popup will show to the right with the title already selected to be changed.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.source: Adding an existing note from the note tree__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Select the desired note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Hold the mouse on the note and drag it to the map to the desired location.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: The map should be updated with the new marker.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: This works for:
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Notes that are not part of the geo map, case in which a __TRILIUM_PH_0__clone__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will be created.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Notes that are a child of the geo map but not yet positioned on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Notes that are a child of the geo map and also positioned, case in which the marker will be relocated to the new position.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Dragging existing notes only works if the map is in editing mode. See the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section for more information.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding an existing note from the note tree

units.source: Adding a note from a place the map already shows__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: When a vector map style is used, the map itself draws the shops, cafés, museums and other places around the area being viewed. Once the map is zoomed in far enough for these to be drawn, they can be clicked:
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Look for the places drawn in orange. This is the same color used for a place found by searching. These are the places you can click. They are drawn almost solid, while the other places on the map stay a faint grey.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Rest the mouse on one of them. Its name appears above it, and the mouse cursor changes to a pointer. The map draws these places as icons without names, so you read a name by hovering over it. If all the names were shown at once, they would crowd out the titles of your own markers.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Click it. The same panel used for a place found by searching appears. It shows the name of the place and its coordinates, and a pin is placed on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add as marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to keep it. The note is created with the name of the place as its title, and with the icon that matches the kind of place it is.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Places are read from the map data that has already been downloaded, so clicking one does not send anything to the internet.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Some things to keep in mind:
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: Places with no name in the map data, such as benches or parking spaces, show no name and cannot be clicked. Clicking them does nothing, just like clicking an empty part of the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: The map's own markers come first. If a marker covers a place, clicking it opens the note and not the place.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: This does not work with the raster (OpenStreetMap) style, because its places are part of the map image. It also does not work with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Neutrino__TRILIUM_PH_1__ style, which draws no places.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: In read-only mode you can still click a place and read it, but you cannot keep it as a marker.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a note from a place the map already shows

units.source: How the location of the markers is stored__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > How the location of the markers is stored

units.source: The location of a marker is stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute of the child notes:
units.context: Geo Map > How the location of the markers is stored

units.source: This value can be added manually if needed. The value of the attribute is made up of the latitude and longitude separated by a comma.
units.context: Geo Map > How the location of the markers is stored

units.source: On an image map, the position is stored in __TRILIUM_PH_0__ instead (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Image maps__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
units.context: Geo Map > How the location of the markers is stored

units.source: Repositioning markers__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: Once a marker is set, it can be repositioned using one of the two ways:
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: By right clicking the marker and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_0__Move to another location__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: By clicking the marker to open the popup and selecting the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Move to another location__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button underneath the title bar.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: After clicking the button to move the marker, click at the desired position on the map to replace it. To cancel the operation, press Escape.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: If the map is locked for editing (see below), the map needs to be unlocked before moving the marker.
units.context: Geo Map > Repositioning markers

units.source: Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes

units.source: Hovering over a marker will display a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tooltip__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with the content of the note it belongs to.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes

units.source: Clicking on the note title in the tooltip will navigate to the note in the current view.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes

units.source: Right-clicking the marker will open a contextual menu (as described below).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes

units.source: Clicking a marker will focus on the marker and display a dedicated popup with the details. This works regardless of whether the map is editable or not.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes

units.source: Popup view__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: When a marker, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__shape__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or track is clicked, a popup will open to the right which contains the following information:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: The title and icon of the marker, both editable.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: An indicator for the coordinates (__TRILIUM_PH_0__); clicking it will copy the coordinates to clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to maximize the popup.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Buttons to interact with the current item:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Open the marker in the same pane, or use __TRILIUM_PH_1__ to open it in a new tab, split, etc.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to open the location in a dedicated application (e.g. Google Maps on mobile).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Color picker to change the color of the marker.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Markers can also be moved, unlike tracks or shapes (which need to be redrawn).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Button to remove the marker from the map, which can optionally delete its corresponding note.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Removing a marker without deleting the note will only remove its __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute (case in which the coordinates have to be manually added back in in order to get the note to show on the map again).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Similarly, removing a shape will remove its __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the marker, if any.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: The note's content which can be edited directly from the panel.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: To dismiss the popup:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Press the X button at the top-right of the popup.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: In the map, press anywhere outside the popup.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Or simply press the Escape key.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: When a marker is clicked, the map will automatically adjust the viewport so that the marker is still visible with the popup open. The currently selected marker is shown slightly bigger.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: It is possible to switch between markers by clicking on them even when the popup view is already open.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Markers can have __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ between them and clicking on such a link will automatically adjust the viewport and the popup view to the new note.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Popup view

units.source: Contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: It's possible to press the right mouse button to display a contextual menu.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: If right-clicking an empty section of the map (not on a marker), it allows to:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Displays the latitude and longitude. Clicking this option will copy them to the clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Open the location using an external application (if the operating system supports it).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Adding a new marker at that location.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: If right-clicking on a marker, it allows to:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Displays the latitude and longitude. Clicking this option will copy them to the clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Open the location using an external application (if the operating system supports it).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: Open the note in a new tab, split or window.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Move the marker to another location.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Button to remove the marker from the map, which can optionally delete its corresponding note. Removing a marker without deleting the note will only remove its __TRILIUM_PH_1__ attribute (case in which the coordinates have to be manually added back in in order to get the note to show on the map again).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: Shapes can also be right-clicked and the menu is similar to markers except they cannot be moved.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Contextual menu

units.source: Icon and color__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Icon and color

units.source: The markers will have the same icon as the note.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Icon and color

units.source: It's possible to add a custom color to a marker by assigning them a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute such as __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Icon and color

units.source: This also applies to tracks and __TRILIUM_PH_0__shapes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Icon and color

units.source: The color as it will be displayed on the map might be slightly tinted in order to make the text or icon more legible.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Icon and color

units.source: Adding the coordinates manually__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually

units.source: Searching for the place is usually quicker (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Searching the map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ above). The steps below remain useful for a coordinate that is already to hand, or for a place the search cannot find.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually

units.source: In a nutshell, create a child note and set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute to the coordinates.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually

units.source: The value of the attribute is made up of the latitude and longitude separated by a comma.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually

units.source: Adding from Google Maps__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: In Google Maps, on the web:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: Look for a desired location, right click on it and a context menu will show up.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: Simply click on the first item displaying the coordinates and they will be copied to clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: In Trilium, create a child note under the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: Then paste the value inside the text box into the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute of a child note of the map (don't forget to surround the value with a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ character).
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from Google Maps

units.source: Adding from OpenStreetMap__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from OpenStreetMap

units.source: Similarly to the Google Maps approach:
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from OpenStreetMap

units.source: Go to any location on openstreetmap.org and right click to bring up the context menu. Select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show address__TRILIUM_PH_1__ item.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from OpenStreetMap

units.source: The address will be visible in the top-left of the screen, in the place of the search bar. Select the coordinates and copy them into the clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from OpenStreetMap

units.source: Simply paste the value inside the text box into the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute of a child note of the map and then it should be displayed on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Interaction with the markers, tracks or shapes > Adding the coordinates manually > Adding from OpenStreetMap

units.source: Drawing shapes on the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Drawing shapes on the map

units.source: See the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__Drawing shapes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ page.
units.context: Geo Map > Drawing shapes on the map

units.source: Using an image instead of the world map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Using an image instead of the world map

units.source: A geo map can be drawn over an image of your own, such as a floor plan or a fantasy map, with markers placed in the image's pixels. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Image maps__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Geo Map > Using an image instead of the world map

units.source: Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: Trilium can display GPS tracks on the geo map, in the form of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ files.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: To add a track, either:
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: Drag & drop a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ file inside the geo map in the note tree.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: In order for the file to be recognized as a GPS track, it needs to show up as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__File type__TRILIUM_PH_2__ field.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add a GPS track from a GPX file__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button which will directly prompt for a GPX file and import it as a subnote of the collection.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: When going back to the map, the track should now be visible.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: The starting point of the track will be displayed as a marker, with the name of the note underneath. The start marker will also respect the icon and the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ of the note. The end marker is displayed with a distinct icon.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: If the track file contains multiple tracks, they will all be displayed as well as markers. Trilium will also split a single track that happens to have non-continuous points.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: If the GPX contains waypoints, they will also be displayed, including their names.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: When the track is clicked, the entire route is brought into view, as well as the right popup will indicate details about the track such as distance, duration and the elevation map. This information is also displayed when clicking the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ note itself.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: When clicking on the markers of a track (whether it's the start or stop builtin markers, or custom markers that are part of the track), only that marker is brought into view, as opposed to the entire route.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding GPS tracks (.gpx)

units.source: Read-only mode__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: When a map is __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ all editing features will be disabled such as:
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the bottom of the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: Repositioning markers.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: Editing from the contextual menu (removing locations or adding new items).
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: Keeping a place as a marker, whether you found it by searching or clicked it on the map. You can still search and click, and you can still look at a place and copy its coordinates.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: Drawing __TRILIUM_PH_0__shapes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog; its entry is hidden from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: To set a map as read-only, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Read-only__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Geo Map > Read-only mode

units.source: Configuration__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration

units.source: Map Style__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The styling of the map can be adjusted in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__, under __TRILIUM_PH_2__Background__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__ dialog, or manually via the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attribute.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The geo map comes with two different types of styles:
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: Raster styles
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: For these styles the map is represented as a grid of images at different zoom levels. This is the traditional way OpenStreetMap used to work.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: Zoom is slightly restricted.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: Currently, the only raster theme is the original OpenStreetMap style.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: Vector styles
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: Vector styles are not represented as images, but as geometrical shapes. This makes the rendering much smoother, especially when zooming and looking at the building edges, for example.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The map can be zoomed in much further.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: These come in various styles that are both light (Colorful, Graybeard, Neutrino) and dark (Eclipse, Shadow).
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The vector styles come from __TRILIUM_PH_0__VersaTiles__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a free and open-source project providing map tiles based on OpenStreetMap.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The VersaTiles layers also provide 3D building information (see below).
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: The default theme is Versatiles Colorful (vector).
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style

units.source: 3D view with buildings__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style > 3D view with buildings

units.source: Trilium v0.105.0 introduces a 3D view, courtesy of MapLibre GL. To enter 3D mode, simply press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__3D__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button at the bottom-right of the map or press Ctrl and drag across the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style > 3D view with buildings

units.source: The buildings will only appear from zoom 14 onwards to avoid lag.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style > 3D view with buildings

units.source: To get 3D buildings, make sure you are using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__VersaTiles__TRILIUM_PH_1__ styles which provide the building informatia via the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ source.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Map Style > 3D view with buildings

units.source: Custom map style / tiles__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Starting with v0.102.0 it is possible to use custom tile sets, but only in raster format.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: To use one:
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Background__TRILIUM_PH_1__, set __TRILIUM_PH_2__Type__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to __TRILIUM_PH_4__Custom tileset__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tile URL__TRILIUM_PH_1__, enter the address of the tile set, with __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__ where the zoom level and the position of the tile go. For example, to use Esri.NatGeoWorldMap, enter __TRILIUM_PH_5____TRILIUM_PH_6____TRILIUM_PH_7__. The URL is saved once you leave the field; a URL that doesn't start with __TRILIUM_PH_8__ or __TRILIUM_PH_9__, or that lacks one of the three placeholders, is not saved. A map drawn over an image keeps its image until a URL is saved.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: If the tiles are dark, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Dark tileset__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which draws the marker titles in a light color so that they remain readable.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Additionally:
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Hi-DPI tiles are supported via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ placeholder.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Servers that number their tiles by quadkey are supported via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ placeholder, in place of __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: To go back to a built-in style, set __TRILIUM_PH_0__Type__TRILIUM_PH_1__ back to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vector & Raster__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The tile set is switched off rather than removed: its label is renamed to __TRILIUM_PH_4__, so setting __TRILIUM_PH_5__Type__TRILIUM_PH_6__ to __TRILIUM_PH_7__Custom tileset__TRILIUM_PH_8__ again brings back the same URL. A tile set inherited from a parent note or a template is overridden by the default style instead.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: The tile set can also be set manually: the URL goes in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__, and the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ label marks it as dark. __TRILIUM_PH_4__ also overrides the built-in styles.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: For a list of tile sets, see the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Leaflet Providers preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ page. Select a desired tile set and just copy the URL from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Plain JavaScript__TRILIUM_PH_3__ example.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Custom vector map support is planned, but not yet implemented.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Custom map style / tiles

units.source: Other options__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The following options can be configured either via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by clicking on the settings (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button. Alternatively, each of these options also have a corresponding __TRILIUM_PH_3__label__TRILIUM_PH_4__ that can be set manually.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: Scale, which illustrates the scale of the map in either kilometers or miles in the bottom-left of the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The unit is determined by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting locale__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The name of the markers is displayed by default underneath the pin on the map. Since v0.102.0, it is possible to hide these labels which increases the performance and decreases clutter when there are many markers on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: v0.105.0 also introduces a feature called __TRILIUM_PH_0__Group nearby markers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which will cluster multiple markers together at low zoom.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The clusters display the number of items they contain. The color also changes based on the count.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: Clicking on a cluster will automatically zoom in so that the individual markers that make up the cluster are now visible.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The same options are also listed under __TRILIUM_PH_0__General__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_4__ dialog, opened from the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_6__ or from the settings menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_7__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_8__. Its __TRILIUM_PH_9__Included notes__TRILIUM_PH_10__ section sets whether archived notes are shown and the __TRILIUM_PH_11__Maximum nesting depth__TRILIUM_PH_12__ (see below), and its __TRILIUM_PH_13__Background__TRILIUM_PH_14__ section holds the map style, the URL of a custom tile set when __TRILIUM_PH_15__Type__TRILIUM_PH_16__ is set to __TRILIUM_PH_17__Custom tileset__TRILIUM_PH_18__ (see above), or, with __TRILIUM_PH_19__Type__TRILIUM_PH_20__ set to __TRILIUM_PH_21__Custom image__TRILIUM_PH_22__, draws the map over an image of your own instead, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_23__Image maps__TRILIUM_PH_24__.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options

units.source: The map shows the notes of its whole subtree, not only its children. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Maximum nesting depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) limits how deep below the map it looks: __TRILIUM_PH_3__ shows only the children, __TRILIUM_PH_4__ adds their children, and so on. Without a value, every level is shown.
units.context: Geo Map > Configuration > Other options
